about: Round 1583. The two host proof behind the four NBA Connections file boards (nbaconn-001 to 004, src/data/nbaConnectionsPuzzles.ts, which are also live rows of nba_connections_puzzles and were current against the lead's 2026-10-29 export). No NBA board had ever been held to two hosts: the file's header said every fact was checked against the site's own tables on 2026-07-21, one source. The record (scripts/data/nbaConnectionsRecord-2026-10.json: ESPN's athlete service and nba.com's player page) is one host and basketball-reference.com (scripts/data/nbaConnectionsSecondHost-2026-10.json) the second; the checker reads both and returns unknown where they disagree. Wikis are never a source. The 16 table rows past the file (nbaconn-005 to 020) are Round 1586's.
rules: A fact names a man, a group label and whether he fits it (holds), and carries two sources on two different hosts, neither a wiki: the record first (site.web.api.espn.com for clubs, totals and birthplaces; nba.com for the draft), basketball-reference.com second. Facts are written by scripts/usConnections/verifyNbaFacts.mjs facts from the two committed host files, and a fact is written only where both hosts give the verdict it records.
Career means NBA regular season only: playoffs never count and ABA totals never count (the second host keeps a man's ABA rows apart).

A club group counts NBA regular season seasons with that club under the name the label gives, up to the season in its date by start year ("as of 2025-26" counts 2025-26 and earlier). ABA seasons never count: a man with ABA seasons for the club whose group is on his board is unknown beside it (critic-1583 item 5) and, a coin toss, leaves that board as a gray pair.

A man with a season under another name of the same franchise (the Minneapolis Lakers beside a Los Angeles Lakers group, the Seattle SuperSonics beside a Thunder group) is unknown beside it until this ledger decides him: a gray pair who leaves the board, or a club label that names both (critic-1583 item 4). A rostered man who played no game for a club (DeMarcus Cousins with the 2019-20 Lakers) is a gray pair beside that club too: a board never hinges on that argument (Round 219's rule).

A birth group reads where a man was born (ESPN's displayBirthPlace, basketball-reference's birthplace line), never a citizenship or nba.com's COUNTRY (Tony Parker: citizenship France, born in Bruges, Belgium).
A draft group reads the overall pick (nba.com's DRAFT_NUMBER and basketball-reference's Draft line); ESPN's draft line gives the pick within its round.
Where the two hosts disagree on a verdict the checker returns unknown and the ceilings (0) turn it red until a third host settles it in the overlay, or the man leaves the board.
watchRules: Written before the first decision. The season in play is 2026-27; the last finished one is 2025-26 (LAST_FINISHED nba 2025 in scripts/simUsConnectionsFacts.mjs).

Still playing: ESPN's active flag, or nba.com's roster status Active, or any season from 2024-25 on (an unsigned veteran can still sign and add to a mark). No retirement is read: a season from 2024-25 on counts as still playing whatever either host says, which can only watch more men, never fewer.

A club group is dated in the trailing "(as of 2025-26)" shape on every board, whether or not a man still playing sits beside it today (one shape on every board; a date can only shrink what a group holds). Section 8 holds it.

A career mark (points, rebounds, assists, three-pointers, steals, blocks, games): a man still playing within one season's worth of it on either host is watched, a season's worth being the most anyone has added in one NBA regular season (basketball-reference's single season leaders pages, read 2026-10-29, the ABA rows set aside): 4,029 points (Wilt Chamberlain, 1961-62), 2,149 rebounds (Wilt Chamberlain, 1960-61), 1,164 assists (John Stockton, 1990-91), 402 three-pointers (Stephen Curry, 2015-16), 301 steals (Alvin Robertson, 1985-86), 456 blocks (Mark Eaton, 1984-85), 88 games (Walt Bellamy, 1968-69). These are bounds of the rule (NBA_REACH in scripts/lib/usConnectionsCheck.mjs), not claims any board makes.
Fixed: the draft (the overall pick) and the birthplace (a country, or a continent).

Only club groups are dated (Round 1574 R4): an award, Hall of Fame, running list or "never" group beside a watched man is fixed by moving the man or rebuilding the group into a finished claim. The four file boards carry none.

otherUnknownNote: Other tiles the record cannot judge against a group beside them: none on the head. The count may only fall.
clubLabelsNote: Each file label covers its club under the name it gives, nothing else (scripts/lib/usConnectionsCheck.mjs NBA_CLUBS). franchiseNames are the other names the franchise played under, from basketball-reference's franchise page (/teams/<code>/, read 2026-10-29): a man with a season under one of them is unknown beside the label, never a no. No man on the four file boards has a season under any of them, on either host. A lineage entry can only make a verdict unknown, never a yes or a no.
decisions: nbaconn-001: the Heat group dated; no member moved.

nbaconn-002: the Bulls group dated. Tony Parker left "Born in France" (born in Belgium on both hosts: Bruges, Belgium on basketball-reference, Belgium on ESPN) for Victor Wembanyama (born in France on both hosts: Paris on ESPN, Le Chesnay on basketball-reference; a Spur only, 400 three-pointers, 2,054 rebounds). Nicolas Batum left it too: 1,842 three-pointers with a 2025-26 season (still playing on the record) puts him a season from "2,000+ career three-pointers". Ian Mahinmi (born in Rouen, France; Spurs, Mavericks, Pacers, Wizards; 8 three-pointers, 2,705 rebounds; last season 2019-20) took his place.
nbaconn-003: the Warriors and Knicks groups dated; no member moved.

nbaconn-004: the Celtics, Lakers and Kings groups dated. DeMarcus Cousins (a gray pair beside the Lakers) left the Kings group for De'Aaron Fox (Kings 2017-18 to 2024-25, then the Spurs; no Celtics or Lakers season on either host; born in the USA on both hosts).
